description: Nos enfundamos en el espíritu de la misión Artemis de la NASA: exploración, rigor técnico y trabajo en equipo. Contamos con experiencia en desarrollo web (PHP, Tailwind CSS, frameworks modernos), arquitectura de software, gestión de bases de datos (SQL) y consumo/integración de APIs REST. Nos apasiona transformar datos complejos e ideas ambiciosas en aplicaciones funcionales, intuitivas y listas para el mundo real.
summary:
We developed a health-monitoring platform for astronauts on space missions. It brings together each crew member's vital signs, sleep, physical activity, radiation exposure and mental well-being, and turns that data into clear, actionable information.

To address the challenge, the platform evaluates every measurement instantly against medical ranges adapted to the mission environment, whether a space station, transit, the Moon or Mars. Results appear on an interactive 3D human body that lights up organ by organ in green, yellow or red. When a value goes out of range, an alert reaches the medical team automatically. The team monitors the whole crew from a single dashboard, sends personalized advice and reviews validated psychological tests. Gamification and daily reminders turn self-care into a habit. Readings come from a device simulator built on real NASA data from the Inspiration4 mission (OSDR) and space-weather activity (DONKI).

This matters because astronauts face unique health risks far from home, often without a doctor nearby. Our platform makes prevention replace reaction: astronauts gain autonomy over their own health, and the medical team can act before small problems become serious ones.
details:
What does your project do, and how does it work?

It is a health-monitoring platform for astronauts on space missions. It brings together their vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, temperature, glucose), their sleep, physical activity, daily radiation dose and mental well-being, and turns that data into clear information for both the crew member and the medical team.

Measurements arrive in two ways: the astronaut logs them, or their devices send them automatically. The system evaluates each value instantly against medical ranges adjusted to the mission environment (space station, transit, Moon or Mars) and classifies it as normal, caution or critical. The result appears on an interactive 3D human body, where every organ takes the color of its current state.

When a value goes out of range, the platform automatically creates an alert for the flight surgeon. From a dashboard covering the whole crew, the surgeon handles alerts, sends personalized advice and reviews the results of validated psychological tests (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PSS-4 andk answer triggers an urgent notification. The platform has three user roles: astronaut, medical team and administration.

What benefits does it have?

- Prevention: it detects early what could be.

- Autonomy: astronauts understand and look after their own bodies without always depending on the doctor.

- Complete oversight: the medical team sees in a single view.

- Healthy habits: points, streaks, badges and daily reminders turn self-care into a routine.
